item.title: Bristol man appears in court over King’s Lynn assault charges
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Bristol man appears in court over King’s Lynn assault charges
A 40-year-old man from Bristol has appeared at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court facing multiple charges, including threats to kill and intentional strangulation. Deepen Banerjee, of Whitchurch Lane, is accused of offences involving his wife at a King’s Lynn address between May 2024 and April of this year. The charges also include assault and engaging in coercive and controlling behaviour.
Mr Banerjee did not enter a plea during Thursday’s hearing. Due to the nature of the allegations, the case has been sent to Norwich Crown Court, where he is due to appear on October 8. He has been released on conditional bail, which prohibits him from contacting the alleged victim.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/man-accused-of-threatening-to-kill-and-strangle-wife-9482478/

item.title: MP opposes potential service cuts at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
MP opposes potential service cuts at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
North West Norfolk MP James Wild has voiced strong opposition to reports suggesting a potential downgrade of A&E, intensive care, and maternity services at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. Mr Wild met with the chief executive of the Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group to express concerns over a lack of transparency regarding a working group currently reviewing long-term service strategies.
The MP argued that removing consultant-led services would be unacceptable for rural communities, citing the impact on ambulance travel times and patient access. A review is expected to report to the hospital group’s board in October. Mr Wild has received assurances that the current review will not jeopardise plans for a new hospital facility.

Former King’s Lynn hospital nurse struck off
A former nurse at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has been removed from the nursing register. Adam Feary was previously convicted of possessing over 14,000 indecent images of children and animals, as well as a manual encouraging sexual offending.
The Nursing and Midwifery Council’s Fitness to Practise Committee concluded that Feary’s actions breached fundamental professional standards. While he received a suspended prison sentence last year, the committee determined that an immediate interim order was necessary to protect the public. Feary, who worked at the hospital until July 2023, has been placed on the sex offenders register for ten years. The Queen Elizabeth Hospital confirmed his employment was terminated following an internal investigation.
